title: SKL - Neubau Eltern-Kind-Zentrum am Städtischen Klinikum Lüneburg
description: Das Städtische Klinikum Lüneburg (SKL) ist ein Krankenhaus der Schwerpunktversorgung. Es versorgt einen zunehmend großen Teil der Bevölkerung im nordöstlichen Niedersachsen und beschäftigt über 1.500 Mitarbeiter. Als akademisches Lehrkrankenhaus des Universitäts-klinikums Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE) ist es mit derzeit 527 Planbetten im Krankenhausbedarfsplan des Landes Niedersachsen ausgewiesen. Das Klinikum verfügt über ein breites medizinisches Leistungsspektrum. Das Städtische Klinikum Lüneburg plant am Standort Lüneburg ein Eltern-Kind-Zentrum als eigenständigen Erweiterungsbaustein der Kinder- und Jugendmedizin sowie der Gynäkologie und Geburtshilfe. Als solches beherbergt es die Entbindungsstation mit sieben Kreißsälen. Weiterhin bildet es, als Bestandteil einer umfassenden Zielplanung - nach Fertigstellung - die Grundlage für weitere zukünftige Erneuerungen am SKL: einen Funktionsbau, unter anderem mit umfangreichem Behandlungs- und Operationsbereich. title: Anskaffelse av rammeavtaler for IT-konsulenter
description: Fiskeridirektoratet ønsker å inngå rammeavtaler for IT-konsulenter innenfor 5 ulike kompetanseområder/kategorier. Vi vil leie inn ønskede ressurser ved behov tilknyttet digitalisering. Det skal inngås flere parallelle rammeavtaler innenfor hvert enkelt av de 5 kompetanseområdene listet opp nedenfor. Tilbyderne som best tilfredsstiller kravene som stilles i kravspesifikasjonen innenfor de ulike kompetanseområdene, blir tildelt kontrakter innenfor det/de enkelte kompetanseområde(ne) der tilbyderen er best kvalifisert. Tilbyder kan levere tilbud i én, flere eller alle kategoriene. Tildeling av rammeavtaler innenfor hvert enkelt kompetanseområde foretas uavhengig av hverandre. Én tilbyder kan dermed bli tildelt flere av de aktuelle rammeavtalene, og for hvert kompetanseområde vil Fiskeridirektoratet tildele rammeavtaler til de 3 beste tilbyderne. For hele anskaffelsen skal det dermed inngås 15 avtaler totalt. Fiskeridirektoratet vil gjennomføre avrop i form av minikonkurranser mellom leverandørene med rammeavtale innenfor det enkelte kompetanseområdet, for å finne den eller de best egnede ressursene for å dekke behovet. Konsulenttjenestene er delt inn i følgende 5 kompetanseområder: 1. Systemutvikling og teknisk testing 2. Teknisk prosjektledelse innen digitalisering og digital transformasjon 3. Dataplattform og informasjonsforvaltning 4. Drift av digital plattform (DevOps/SRE) 5. Lokal drift / skydrift Tjenesten leveres ved at konsulenter innlemmes i våre allerede eksisterende team som har ansvar for både utvikling og drift/monitorering, og bidrar der med sin kompetanse og kapasitet. Rammeavtalene skal i utgangspunktet gjelde fra ca. 10.03.2027 og vil ha en varighet på 1 år, med opsjon på 1+1+1 års forlengelse av avtalene. Anslått totalverdi for hele anskaffelsen er på 250 millioner NOK eks. mva. Behov og verdi vil imidlertid variere innenfor de ulike kompetanseområdene. Se konkurransedokumenter for mer informasjon.

title: Helmet-Mounted First-Person View Display System
description: I. Description USSOCOM is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing dismounted Special Operations Forces with a helmet-mounted first-person view (FPV) display. This display must deliver an expanded field of view, certified ballistic protection, real-time tactical information overlay, and unmanned system control in contested, congested, and all-weather environments. The effort aims to develop a 50-degree field-of-view Display Module that integrates full military ballistic protection, ATAK capability, head tracking, improved display performance, and expanded environmental durability while remaining compatible with existing soldier systems and helmets. This announcement is for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation. The Government will use responses to this notice to assess interest and capability within the industry and to determine the acquisition strategy (e.g., limited competition or small business set-aside). This Sources Sought is posted as a Call to Vulcan and all responses must be submitted to Vulcan. II. Requested Information Interested vendors are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Company name, address, point of contact, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CMMC/NIST (type, date, score), website. Business Size: Indicate your business size and socio-economic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, etc.). Confirm your business size relative to 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Security Clearance: Indicate your current facility clearance and the level of facility security clearances you can maintain. Relevant Experience: Provide a brief overview of your experience in supporting SOF, system testing, commercial integration, and ATAK areas as listed below. If no experience, briefly identify the names and CAGE codes of any small businesses that have demonstrated experience that your company can team/partner with on this requirement. Display Systems. System testing (researching, planning, designing, developing, analyzing, and testing a variety of electronic equipment and systems, military command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems, interface units, and other electronic devices and test equipment) to support enhanced situational awareness, command and control, and precision effects while retaining mobility, protection, and compatibility with existing soldier equipment. Experience with existing soldier equipment (ATAK EUD, radios, hubs). Experience with researching, testing, and integrating emerging technologies as they pertain to real-time overlay of ATAK tactical data, targeting information, and UAS video/control in day, night, and all-weather contested environments. Capability Statement: Submit a capability statement that responds to the following questions: Describe your company�s relevant experience providing SOF support in any of the following areas: ATAK interface, ballistic protection integration, development testing, head tracking sensor integration, software updates and integration, integrating processing hardware and the Display Module into a single module, Windblast compatibility, Expanded environmental envelope, similar requirements or related mission sets. Include contract numbers, customers, and scope. Explain your approach to development milestones (SRR, PDR, CDR, development tests, prototype deliveries) for the combined work scope versus individual items and identify any related any similar efforts. Confirm your company�s ability to maintain adherence to milestones and react to shifts within technology or supply chains to avoid impact to development and enable future scaling of production. Describe your recruiting, screening, and retention strategy for specialized Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Explain how your company would manage and execute a contract for this development. What program management tools, structures, or practices will ensure successful delivery? Describe your Quality Assurance/Quality Control processes and how they would ensure compliance with the Statement of Objectives (SOO), Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) and Key System Attributes (KSAs). If applicable, identify any suppliers, subcontractors or teaming partners. Specify their roles and the percentage of work they are expected to perform. Identify any services within the SOO that meet the definition of commercial services under FAR 2.101. Provide catalog pricing or related contract references. Provide feedback on a recommendation on contract type and structure (length, phases, single award, FFP/CPFF, OTA). Are there any risks or constraints that may affect your participation? Identify how the USSOCOM can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. Identify any condition or action that may be having the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion. Recommendations to improve the approach/specifications/NAICS/PSC/ DRAFT SOO to acquiring the identified items/services. III. Submission Details Submission Deadline: 3:00 Eastern on 01-DEC-2026 Submission Location: All submissions shall be made within https://vulcan-sof.com/ Submit To: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=a26a99ef-c351-464f-af93-dbcc064df521 IV. Disclaimer This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal. Responses will not be returned, and the Government will not reimburse costs incurred in response preparation. Participation in this notice is not a guarantee of future contract award.

buyer: Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire IFSN
title: (26163) 998 Partenaire technique WEB
description:
L'Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire (IFSN) est tenue de fournir des informations au public et aux autorités. Le site web de l'IFSN met à la disposition du public toutes les informations pertinentes et comprend une rubrique « Actualités » ainsi que des contenus statiques tels que des pages, des documents et le Forum technique.


Le site web respecte les directives de la Confédération en matière d’identité visuelle (CI) et de conception (CD) et est multilingue (allemand, français, italien et anglais). Des contenus sont également disponibles en « langue simplifiée » et en « langue des signes ».


L’IFSN exploite les trois sites web ENSI, ENSI-RAT et EGT-Suisse sur une base technique uniforme avec une configuration WordPress multisite, un design cohérent, des plugins spécifiques à l’IFSN et des interfaces vers des systèmes externes. L’infrastructure d’hébergement, dotée de différents environnements de développement, garantit un fonctionnement sécurisé.


L’appel d’offres a pour objectif le changement de partenaire technique et d’hébergement, ainsi que la mise en place d’un « darksite » autonome pouvant être activé en cas d’urgence ou de crise.


Nous recherchons un partenaire technique chargé de l’exploitation sécurisée, de la maintenance et du développement de l’infrastructure technique. Cela comprend la gestion des sites web existants, la migration vers un partenaire d’hébergement adapté, ainsi que la gestion de projet et la mise en œuvre du « darksite ».

buyer: Secrétariat d’État à l’économie (SECO) - Direction de la promotion économique
title: regiosuisse : prestations de communication, site web et Events
description:
Le présent appel d’offres et les prestations qui y sont liées contribuent à la mise en œuvre du mandat du Centre du réseau de développement régional regiosuisse (ci-après « regiosuisse ») entre janvier 2028 et juin 2032. Ces prestations complètent celles du Lot1 du mandat regiosuisse attribué en 2023 (prestations regiosuisse « Direction, manifestations riches en contenus informatifs et analyses »), qui s’étend également jusqu’en 2032. Outre la direction du mandat, la majeure partie des prestations concernent la mise en œuvre de supports de communication, notamment via le site web regiosuisse.ch, ainsi que l’organisation d’Events.

Fondée en 2008, regiosuisse s’est imposé comme un acteur majeur dans le domaine de la gestion et de la diffusion des connaissances en matière de développement régional, ainsi que dans la mise en réseau des acteurs concernés. La Nouvelle politique régionale (NPR) a été au cœur de sa mission dès le début. Le Secrétariat d’État à l’économie (SECO) est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la NPR et, par conséquent, de la mission de regiosuisse. À partir de 2016, la gestion des connaissances liée à la politique des agglomérations (AggloPol) et à la politique pour les espaces ruraux et les régions de montagne (PERM) a été intégrée dans la convention de prestations conclue avec regiosuisse.

El dossier deberá contener, según resulte aplicable a cada elemento, fotografías, fichas o descripciones técnicas, dimensiones, características constructivas y funcionales, materiales, acabados y cuantos otros datos resulten necesarios para comprobar que los bienes propuestos cumplen las prescripciones mínimas establecidas en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas particulares. En particular, deberá permitir comprobar la adecuación técnica de los principales elementos integrantes del suministro: casetas de madera; elementos luminosos y ornamentales; caseta de Papá Noel y jaima; photocall; árbol de Navidad; pórtico ornamental de bienvenida; letras corporativas iluminadas; escenario; instalación eléctrica temporal; elementos de señalización y protección contra incendios; y aseos portátiles, incluidos los adaptados. La documentación aportada deberá permitir al órgano de contratación comprobar que los bienes que se adscribirán a la ejecución del contrato cumplen las características mínimas exigidas. La falta de presentación de esta documentación por la persona o entidad propuesta como adjudicataria, o su insuficiencia para acreditar el cumplimiento de las especificaciones técnicas mínimas, determinará las consecuencias previstas en la LCSP para la falta de acreditación de los requisitos exigidos con carácter previo a la adjudicación. La solvencia técnica exigida no se fundamenta en la experiencia previa de la persona o entidad licitadora ni se exige una relación de suministros anteriormente ejecutados. En consecuencia, los medios de acreditación establecidos en esta cláusula resultan igualmente aplicables a las empresas de nueva creación, sin necesidad de establecer medios alternativos específicos para estas.

description: Europese Openbare aanbesteding Raamovereenkomst Afrasteringen Aanleiding voor deze aanbestedingsprocedure is het van rechtswege aflopen per 1 februari 2027 van de huidige Raamovereenkomsten. WSRL is voornemens nieuwe Raamovereenkomsten aan te gaan. In onderstaande opsomming worden de afrasteringen nader gespecificeerd evenals de geschatte volumes per jaar. Specificatie afrasteringen en geschatte volumes per jaar: Raster herstelwerk Schapengaas zware Ursus (of gelijkwaardig) met betonnen palen - 500 meter Schapengaas zware Ursus (of gelijkwaardig) met houten palen - 1500 meter Puntdraad met betonnen palen - 500 meter Puntdraad met houten palen - 500 meter Raster nieuw te plaatsen Schapengaas zware Ursus (of gelijkwaardig) met houten palen - 5000 meter Puntdraad met houten palen - 1000 meter Gladde draad met houten palen - 500 meter Aan bovenstaande genoemde volumes kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend. Bijkomende kleine werkzaamheden gerelateerd aan het plaatsen en of herstellen van afrasteringen maken deel uit van deze raamovereenkomst. Looptijd De Raamovereenkomst gaat in op 1 februari 2027 en loopt tot en met 31 januari 2029. Zrekonstruovány budou rovněž všechny kanalizační přípojky ve veřejném prostranství o profilu DN 150 až DN 400 a v celkové délce 587,1 m a přípojky k dešťovým svodům v profilech KT DN 125 – DN 150 v celkové délce 279,5 m. Vodovod a vodovodní přípojky Bude provedena rekonstrukce vodovodu z tvárné litiny s těžkou protikorozní ochranou v celkové délce 881,7 m (v profilu DN 300 v délce 442 m, v profilu DN 250 v délce 269 m , v profilu DN 150 v dílce 170m). Po dobu stavby vodovodu bude náhradní zásobování vodou zajištěno prostřednictvím provizorního vodovodu z ocelových trub Ø 273x6,3 mm a délce 442 m a z ocelových trub Ø 219x8,0 mm v délce 269 m. V rámci stavby budou rekonstruovány vodovodní přípojky DN50, DN80 a DN100 v celkové délce 304,7 m. Hydrovrty V rámci stavby bude rekonstruovaná kanalizace v úseku Š953304 – Š7 a Š994565 – Š4 realizována za trvalého hloubkového odvodňování, a to soustavou hydrovrtů hl. 10 m a v počtu 29 ks. Rekonstrukce VO, přeložky sítí Součástí rekonstrukce ulice Pekařské je dále přeložka stávajícího veřejného osvětlení, dále přeložky sítí (CETIN, MU, Vodafone, T-mobile, FASTER, sdělovacích kabelů DPMB). Tramvajová trať Součástí stavby bude přeložka dvoukolejné tramvajové trati na velkoplošných železobetonových panelech s usazením žlábkové kolejnice NT1 a NT3, v úseku od křižovatky s ulicí Úvoz až po zastávku Šilingrovo náměstí. Součástí přeložky tramvajové trati je realizace 2 ks zastávek, 22 trakčních stožárů, přeložka trolejového vedení, kabelové sítě, přívodních kabelů ELP a přípojek NN pro ELP. Tramvajová trať bude realizována v celkové délce cca 653,50 m. Parametry pro obnovení kolejové dráhy musí plně respektovat vnitřní směrnice Dopravního podniku města Brna, a.s. (dále „DPMB“): • směrnice T07 „TECHNICKÉ PODMÍNKY PRO VÝSTAVBU, REKONSTRUKCE A ÚDRŽBU TRAKČNÍCH VEDENÍ DPMB“ v platném znění. • směrnice T08 „TECHNICKÉ PODMÍNKY PRO PROVOZ A ÚDRŽBU TRAMVAJOVÝCH TRATÍ DPMB“ v platném znění • směrnice T09 „TECHNICKÉ PODMÍNKY PRO VÝSTAVBU A REKONSTRUKCE TRAMVAJOVÝCH TRATÍ DPMB“ v platném znění. Tato směrnice stanovuje technické podmínky pro veškeré rekonstrukce a výstavbu nových tramvajových tratí, resp. kolejové konstrukce a křižovatky, které jsou ve vlastnictví DPMB, případně jsou připravovány a projektovány za účelem budoucího vlastnictví DPMB. Komunikace Součástí je rovněž rozsáhlé provedení celoplošné obnovy komunikačních ploch a chodníků o ploše 16 420 m2. Výstavba bude prováděna po ucelených částech. Podrobný rozsah prací na komunikačních plochách je popsán v dokladové části. Dále bude provedena rekonstrukce stávajícího světelného signalizačního zařízení (SSZ) křižovatky Úvoz – Pekařská. V rámci rekonstrukce bude také realizován mobiliář (lavičky, mříže ke stromům, odpadkové koše, zástěny na odpad, zahrazovací sloupky, stojany na kola, přístřešky MHD, pítka). Stavbu je nutné koordinovat s následujícími akcemi: • Rezidence Anenská brána (investor RUBELA, a.s.) • Reko MS Brno – Pekařská (investor GasNet, s.r.o.) • D1 - Nový laboratorní objekt (investor FNUSA) Zhotovitel je povinen zajistit: • nepřetržitý přístup a příjezd vozidel IZS do Fakultní nemocnice u sv. Anny, • průjezdnost křižovatky Úvoz x Pekařská pro veřejnou dopravu viz POV, • nepřetržitý vjezd a výjezd na pozemek p.č. 1728, k.ú. Staré Brno, • u stavebních objektů SO 452 Sdělovací kabely MU, SO 453 Sdělovací kabely VODAFONE, SO 454 Sdělovací kabely T-MOBILE, SO 455 Sdělovací kabely FASTER a SO 456 Sdělovací kabely DPMB, objednatel upozorňuje na přísné podmínky jednotlivých vlastníků sítí elektronických komunikací. Zhotovitel je povinen zajistit přeložky a zabezpečení podzemních vedení sítí elektronických komunikací tak, aby za celou dobu realizace překládky nedošlo k přerušení provozu infrastruktury, s tím, že přerušení provozu infrastruktury u každého jednotlivého přepojení kabelů infrastruktury nesmí překročit 8 hodin. Podrobný popis rozsahu požadovaných prací je uveden v projektové dokumentaci „Brno, Pekařská – rekonstrukce kanalizace a vodovodu“, vypracované společností PK OSSENDORF s.r.o. title: Pelastuslaitosten virkavaatteet
description: Pelastuslaitosten virkavaatteet Hankinnan kohteena on pelastuslaitosten virkavaatteet tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä määritellyn mukaisesti. Virkavaatteiden hankinta toteutetaan hankintarenkaana, jossa Pohjois-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue (Pohde) vastaa valtuutettuna hankinnasta. Hankintarenkaassa on mukana 26 organisaatiosta, jotka koostuvat hyvinvointialueista, pelastuslaitoksista, Uudenmaan pelastusliitosta, Pelastusopistosta, Sisäministeriöstä, Lupa- ja valvontavirastosta sekä Finlands Svenska Brand- & Räddingsförbund:sta. Tarkka lista hankintayksiköistä löytyy hankintasopimuksesta. Pelastusviranomaisen on käytettävä virkatehtävissään pelastustoimen virkapukua, jollei virkatehtävän laatu tai luonne muuta edellytä. Pelastuslaitoksen muun henkilöstön velvollisuudesta käyttää pelastustoimen virkapukua päättää pelastuslaitos. Pelastustoimen virkapukua käytetään Pelastusopiston henkilöstön virkapukuna ja Pelastusopiston opiskelijoiden opiskelijapukuna. Pelastustoimen virkapukuun kuuluva vaatetus, asusteet ja varusteet on määritelty virkapukuasetuksessa ja tarkemmin pelastustoimen virkapuvun tuotekuvausohjeessa. Virkapuvun käyttöön liittyvä ohjeistus määritellään pelastustoimen virkapukuohjeessa. Pelastustoimen virkapukuun kuuluvat vaatteet, asusteet ja varusteet on jaettu virkapukuasetuksessa neljään asukokonaisuuteen: asemavaatetus, toimistovaatetus, vierailuvaatetus ja juhlavaatetus. Virkapukuasetuksessa määritellään, mitä merkkejä ja tunnuksia virkapukuun kuuluvissa varusteissa käytetään ja mihin ne kiinnitetään. Virkapuvussa käytetään vain asetuksessa ja ohjeessa määriteltyjä merkkejä ja tunnuksia. Virkapukujen ja tunnusten tuotekuvaukset on esitetty liitteessä 1.1 Pelastustoimen virkapuvun tuotekuvausohje 2025. Osatarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Hankinnan kohteesta poikkeavia vaihtoehtoisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä. SOPIMUSKAUSI Tämän hetkisen arvion mukaan sopimus tulee voimaan maaliskuussa 2027. Sopimuskauden pituus on viisi vuotta. Sopimuskauden alussa varataan aikaa sopimuksen käyttöönotolle, joka pitää sisällään materiaalien hankinnan ja tuotteiden hyväksynnän. Sopimuksen käyttöönottoon varataan kokonaisuudessaan noin kahdeksan (8) - yhdeksän (9) kuukautta aikaa. Sopimuskauden aikana tehdään reklamaatioiden ja/tai palautteiden pohjalta tuotekehitystyötä mm. materiaalien ja mitoitusten osalta. Sopimuskauden viimeisen kuuden kuukauden aikana varastot ajetaan alas portaittain, jolloin toimitusvarmuus heikkenee. Varsinais-Suomen hyvinvointialue on mukana hankintarenkaassa, mutta tekee hankinnassa oman hankintapäätöksen sekä hankintasopimuksen. TUOTTEISIIN TUTUSTUMINEN Tarjoajalla on mahdollisuus tutustua tuotteisiin 16.11. klo 9:30-11:30 välisenä aikana tai klo 12–14 välisenä aikana. Mikäli annetut ajankohdat eivät sovi, voi Tilaaja mahdollisuuksien mukaan tarjota toista aikaa viikolle 47. title: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI): ELDERS AND ELDER HELPERS FOR CORRECTIONAL SERVICE OF CANADA INSTITUTIONS IN THE PRAIRIES REGION
description: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI): ELDERS AND ELDER HELPERS FOR CORRECTIONAL SERVICE OF CANADA INSTITUTIONS IN THE PRAIRIES REGION PURPOSE OF THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) is asking Elders and Elder Helpers interested in providing Indigenous cultural support and guidance to offenders to contact the CSC Representative identified below. BACKGROUND: CSC has a legal obligation to provide Indigenous offenders with programs and reintegration support that respect Indigenous culture and values. Elders and Elder Helpers provide services under contract to CSC to assist Indigenous offenders in their traditional healing journey, to develop an understanding of traditional Indigenous culture through teachings, guidance, counselling. CSC is committed to providing a variety of rehabilitation programs and opportunities to Indigenous offenders. Elders and Elder Helpers expose individuals and groups of offenders to traditional Indigenous ways of life, based on their own teachings, counselling and traditional ceremonies and practices to promote ongoing healing and balance, and increase the likelihood of successful reintegration. CSC relies on support from First Nation communities, Metis communities, Inuit communities and Indigenous organizations to provide cultural immersion and practices to Indigenous offenders that CSC cannot offer or manage. The Canadian Federal Correctional environment presents challenges in trying to offer Indigenous support and services within institutions due to the constraints of various security levels, the related level of controlled movement of offenders, and other security requirements. CSC has developed policy and guidelines to better support cultural practices and ceremonies. REQUIREMENTS: CSC respects the cultural and traditions of Indigenous communities and strives to treat Elders and Elder Helpers with the utmost respect. Any Elder or Elder Helper interested in providing services to indigenous offenders must be recognized by their Indigenous community as having the knowledge and understanding of the community’s traditional culture, including their ceremonies, protocols, teachings and healing practices, according to their beliefs and social traditions. Knowledge and wisdom are the essential and defining traits Elders and Elder Helpers achieve by following a traditional way of life consistent with the teachings of their community’s Elders and healers over a significant period. Elders and Elder Helpers must be recognized as such by Indigenous communities, other Elders and their teachers. The tasks Elders within CSC typically perform include counselling, teachings, ceremonies and activities for individuals and groups such as: - Providing guidance and teachings through group sessions (circles) and individual discussions with offenders in the institution. - Conducting spiritual services and various traditional ceremonies based on each Elder’s teachings. - Assisting offenders following a healing path in support of their correctional plan. - Escorting offenders on Escorted Temporary Absences (ETAs) for ceremonial and other spiritual purposes as requested and mutually agreed upon. - Providing advice and information to staff and management, locally, regionally and nationally on issues of Indigenous spirituality, cultural practices, ceremonies, ceremonial objects, traditional practices and protocols, traditional medicine or sacred grounds within the institution. This includes the collection and storage of ceremonial objects and traditional and ceremonial medicines. - Introducing institutional staff to various elements of traditional spirituality as deemed appropriate based on the Elder’s teachings. - Participating in case conferences as requested and providing verbal comments to the offender’s Case Management Team regarding the offender’s participation in a healing path and cultural involvement. Elder Helpers within CSC support and assist Elders to facilitate delivery of services and provide support, such as: - Ensuring offenders and staff follow appropriate protocols when approaching the Elder - Ensuring there are adequate supplies of traditional and ceremonial items, materials and medicines for ceremony purposes as requested by the Elder - Coordinating and providing supervision of offenders during ceremonies and assistance at the Elder’s request. Providing performance of ceremonies in the Elder’s absence. This also includes scheduling of ceremonies and providing notification of participants to Elders and staff as required. - Conducting group discussions and teachings, with the Elder’s agreement, in the identification and proper use of ceremonial objects to offenders and staff. - Assisting the Elder in preparing written and verbal reports to support case management teams and participating in staff meetings. - Providing counselling services as directed when the Elder is unavailable. - Providing cultural awareness sessions to staff to promote a culturally safe environment. CONSTRAINTS: Characteristics of the offender population: Along with recognizing the gender, cultural, religious and linguistic differences of inmates, Elders and Elder Helpers must particularly take into consideration the historical context of the lives of Canada’s Indigenous peoples and be sensitive to the impacts of intergenerational trauma and the physical, mental, emotional, and social harms experienced by Indigenous people. Security: As Elders or Elder Helpers under contract to CSC have access to protected information and provide cultural support and guidance within correctional facilities, they are subject to security requirements. They must take measures to protect shared personal and protected information in accordance with the contract’s security requirements. Insurance: Elder and Elder Helpers must comply with CSC’s insurance requirements including Commercial General Liability Insurance and maintain it through the duration of the contract. SUPPORT TO CONTRACTOR: To support Elders and Elder Helpers in providing services to Indigenous Offenders, CSC provides the following: 1. Appropriately equipped facilities for the provision of confidential spiritual services, including the designation of (private) indoor and outdoor space to conduct traditional ceremonies, spiritual activities, and one on one counselling. 2. Ensuring financial and human resources are provided for the gathering of ceremonial objects outside the institution. 3. Ensuring Indigenous Liaison Officers or Parole Officers are available to assist Elders and Elder Helpers in documenting verbal reports Elders and Elder Helpers provide and ensuring the completion of Elder Reviews as per the outline in Commissioner Directive 702 (i.e. Intake, Progress and Decision). 4. Providing orientation to the institution, including all policies and security requirements Elders and Elder Helpers have to follow when carrying out their tasks. 5. Ensuring Elders Elder Helpers are paired with offenders with the same language requirements (French or English). ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS Elders and Elder Helpers providing services to CSC offenders must meet the following essential requirements. CSC reserves the right to modify any and all of these requirements at any time in accordance with its needs. 1. The Elder or Elder Helper must be recognized by their community as an Elder/Elder Helper/Cultural Advisor within that community. 2. The Elder or Elder Helper must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience obtained in the past 10 years in delivering spiritual and cultural services and teachings to Indigenous people. This experience must include: a) providing counselling and guidance according to the traditions and teachings of their own community; and b) being familiar with and able to conduct a variety of ceremonies with a focus on healing according to their own teachings. 3. title: Fire Alarm BPA Fort Drum NY
description: This synopsis is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for quote and no solicitation exists. The Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Drum, NY is seeking multiple businesses willing to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for services under North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 561321: Security Systems Services index Fire alarm sales combined with installation, repair, or monitoring services. The small business size standard for this industry is $22.0 million in average annual revenue. Fire Alarm projects would include but are not limited to the following: providing all necessary resources, management, personnel, materials, transportation, supplies, and equipment, except Government Furnished Property (GFP), necessary in repairing, replacing, and reprogramming of fire alarm systems, sprinkler system, security systems, facility access control systems and all associated equipment in facilities on Fort Drum, NY. Insurance is required for these types of projects; a current certification of insurance must be provided prior to receiving a BPA. Some BPA calls may be posted to UNISON, while not required it is encouraged for vendors receiving a BPA to register at UNISON. Registration is free and can be completed at https://www.unisonglobal.com/product-suites/acquisition/marketplace/ Generally some calls placed will be below $25,000, and may be sporadic in nature. The Contractor must be able to accept the Government Purchase Card (GPC) and submit invoices in Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). To register and access WAWF, go to https://wawf.eb.mil/. BPAs will be evaluated annually and may remain in place for up to five years. IAW FAR 52.204-7 interested parties must be registered with the System for Award Management Registration (SAM) under NACIS code 561621. The registrations can be done through System for Award Management (SAM) for free at https://www.sam.gov The Contractor will not receive a BPA until these registrations are completed. Any interested party should submit their DUNS number, CAGE Code, and Tax ID number to SFC Timmons at david.b.timmons.mil@army.mil. Any correspondence relating to this synopsis should have FIRE ALARM BPA notated in the subject field.

title: VI DPC A34(1) � Veterans Drive Contract 2 Improvements to RTE 30
description: Proposals from all Business Concerns will be accepted for Project VI DPC A34(1) � Veterans Drive Contract 2 Improvements to RTE 30. Solicitation Number 693C73-27-R-000012, located in St. Thomas, USVI. The project consists of the reconstruction and addition of new lanes for a continuous four-lane roadway with two lanes in each direction for an approximate distance of 2052 ft. (0.39 mi). The work includes widening and reconstruction of Veterans Drive, enhance pedestrian and vehicular safety, and improve drainage of the roadway and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost for all the work schedules is estimated to be between $80,000,000 to $90,000,000. Contract Award/Notice to Proceed is subject to the receipt of permits. Proposal documents should be issued on or about November 19, 2026. Proposal due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit a technical proposal in addition to cost proposal. The Solicitation will include further information on these requirements. Use Internet address www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will no longer be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. IMPORTANT SUBCONTRACTING PLAN REQUIREMENTS For purposes of this Contract, the DBE subcontracting goal is 32.10 percent (%) as determined by the Virgin Islands Department of Public Works (VIDPW) with the concurrence of the Contracting Officer. This Contract will be awarded only to the responsive and responsible Offeror who meets this goal or who demonstrates good faith efforts to do so. Failure to make a good faith effort is defined as willful or intentional failure to perform in accordance with the requirements of this Contract, or willful or intentional action to frustrate the achievement of the Subcontracting Plan, if applicable. Guidance on what constitutes good faith efforts is described in the VIDPW's approved DBE Program. Copies of the program can be obtained from the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer. For copies of the current DBE Directory contact the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer. The Contracting Officer, the Contracting Officer�s Representative, and the VIDPW's DBE Liaison Officer are responsible for approving a reasonable and realistic plan. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait for a Government employee from Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD). A Government employee will collect all proposals. Please Note: This solicitation is a Request for Proposal (RFP). Therefore, there will not be a public bid opening and proposals are not available for review.

title: Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) Hardware and Software Production
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Mission Systems is issuing a Full and Open Competitive Solicitation (N00024-26-R-5246) for the development, production, integration, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of the U.S. Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) Hardware and Software. This procurement supports PAE Mission Systems structure, the acronym �PMW/A� means Program Manager, Warfighting / Applications (PMW/A 520) Navigation Program requirements for both surface and subsurface platforms. title: Germany – Trousers – Lieferung von Einsatzbekleidung SEK/MEK
description: Dem LZN obliegt die Beschaffung von Waren und Dienstleistungen für die unmittelbare niedersächsische Landesverwaltung (vgl. § 2 der Betriebsanweisung des LZN). Mit Zustimmung seiner Aufsichtsbehörde kann das LZN weitere Aufgaben für öffentlich-rechtliche Bedarfsträger innerhalb und außerhalb der niedersächsischen Landesverwaltung sowie für privatrechtliche Gesellschaften in vollständiger Eigentümerschaft der öffentlichen Hand übernehmen (vgl. § 3 Betriebsanweisung). In dieser Zuständigkeit umfasst der Auftrag den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Unternehmen (§ 21 VgV) über die Lieferung von Einsatzbekleidung SEK/MEK für Kooperation der Polizei der norddeutschen Küstenländer und die Kunden des LZN gem. beigefügter Auftraggeberliste. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind den technischen Lieferbedingungen und dem Angebotsvordruck zu entnehmen.

title: Objektplanung - BBS I, Umsetzung Brandschutzkonzept
description: Die Stadt Delmenhorst hat aufgrund von festgestellten Mängeln bei einer Brandschutzbegehung ein Brandschutzkonzept in Auftrag gegeben. Dieses soll nun bauordnungsrechtlich genehmigt werden und die darin beschriebenen Brandschutzmaßnahmen geplant und umgesetzt werden. Für die Planung der technischen Anlagen in den Gebäuden (Brandwarnanlage, Hausalarmierungsanlage, Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen und elektrische Leitungsanlagen) wird ein Fachplaner hinzugezogen. Für die erforderlichen Maßnahmen wurde im Rahmen des Brandschutzkonzeptes eine Priorisierungsliste erstellt. Die Hauptmaßnahmen hieraus sind die Errichtung von zwei notwendigen Außentreppen als bauliche 2. Flucht- und Rettungswege, die Ertüchtigung der Hausalarmierungsanlage des Hauptgebäudes auf eine Brandwarnanlage mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, der Einbau einer Hausalarmierungsanlage im Nebengebäude, Einbau von Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Ausführung elektrischer Leitungsanlagen mit Funktionserhalt, Herstellung einer Rauchableitung mit Auslösestellen in einem Treppenraum, Herstellen einer Rauchableitung für den Aufzugschacht im Dach und weitere diverse Brandschutzmaßnahmen, wie z.B. der Austausch von Türen und Verglasungen mit brandschutztechnischer Anforderung oder ein Verschließen ehemaliger Türöffnungen. In bestimmten Bereichen sind Bauteile auf ihre Brandschutzqualität zu überprüfen und ggf. zu ertüchtigen oder in geforderter Qualität zu errichten, dies betrifft insbesondere Leitungsdurchführungen und deren Schottung, Installationsschächte, Entlüftungseinrichtungen innenliegender Bäder und Anschlusspunkte im Bereich der Dächer.

title: PSIB W3048-20KF46 Multipurpose Alpine Military Mobility Training Facility
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and Buyandsell posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted on 2027-01-14 by 2:00 P.M. EST. All bids submitted after 2:00 P.M. EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. The Department of National Defence (DND) has a requirement for a Contractor to provide the facilities, instructors and equipment to conduct training exercises for up to 14 soldiers in Canada. The training will be focused on the use of various transportation types ranging from person-borne equipment such as skis, to motorized equipment such as snowmobiles and motorcycles, in mountainous and austere terrain during all weather conditions. title: APN - Canadian Patrol Submarine Project, CFB Halifax, NS
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE CANADIAN PATROL SUBMARINE PROJECT Halifax, NS (with Security Requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Halifax, NS. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested [contractors and consultants] to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: HX26CPSP; Title: Canadian Patrol Submarine Project - Infrastructure Approximate Estimate:  $5B-$10B Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Following the Prime Minister’s announcement on 6 July 2026, Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS) was selected as the preferred supplier to begin negotiations for delivering Canada’s next fleet of submarines. DND needs to be ready with the appropriate enabling infrastructure synchronized with submarine delivery, with boats arriving 2035 or earlier. To support the delivery of the new submarines, DND must deliver complex, multi-site infrastructure at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Halifax at Wright’s Cove by 2033 to enable submarine berthing and maintenance beginning in 2034. The Construction Management (CM) contract will see the construction of jetties, maintenance facilities, training facilities, offices, and a variety of other supporting facilities to support submarine operations and sustainment. This effort will be realized via the execution of a series of successive work packages in Halifax, NS. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This opportunity is restricted to Canadian, German, and Norwegian firms that meet the security clearance requirements. To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is FACILITY SECURITY CLEARANCE (FSC) at up to level II (SECRET)  4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors  to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Veronica Mendoza Team Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 902-943-1204 Veronica.Mendoza@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: Totalberedskap på tvers av landegrenser - Kommuner og fylkeskommuner i grenseoverskridende samhandling for styrket beredskap og motstandskraft. KS ønsker å utrede hvilket potensial som ligger i å utvikle totalberedskap gjennom samarbeid på tvers av landegrensene, og ønsker tilbud på et FoU-prosjekt som skal svare ut følgende problemstillinger: - Hvordan kan kommuner/fylkeskommuner på norsk og svensk side utvikle et felles rammeverk for beredskap og krisehåndtering som sikrer effektiv samhandling ved grenseoverskridende hendelser? - Hvilke potensielle gevinster vil et slikt utvidet samarbeid over grensen på beredskapsområdet gi for kommuner, fylkeskommuner, innbyggerne og andre beredskapsak. Herunder spesielt se på hvordan kommunenes operative redningsressurs brann og redning kan bidra til å styrke kommunenes samlede beredskapsevne på tvers av landegrensene, spesielt i situasjoner høyt i krisespekteret.

title: D--USGS L10 MOC & Operations Updates
description: Following the May 2026 RFI feedback and one-on-one meetings with industry, the USGS has matured its acquisition strategy for the Landsat 10 Mission Operations Center and Flight Operations scope of work. USGS intends to procure a new commercial, cloud-based or containerized cloud-native MOC to be hosted using USGS's Cloud Hosting Services (CHS) III services or EROS mission infrastructure Container (Kubernetes) Hosting Solution, respectively. Based on industry feedback and technical study results, the Government is no longer considering the option to augment the existing Landsat 8 and 9 LMOC. Included in this announcement are the following reference materials: 1) Draft MOC/Ops Synopsis Document 2) Draft MOC Requirements Document The Government is not requesting feedback at this time; industry will have an opportunity to provide feedback when the Draft RFP is released. These draft documents build on feedback received in response to the May 2026 RFI and provide industry with additional technical detail to clarify the Government's current approach to the Landsat 10 MOC Development and Operations scope of work. These documents will continue to be refined following the spacecraft award and feedback on the draft RFP leading up to the final RFP release. The MOC functions document previously shared with the RFI has been incorporated into the MOC Synopsis and will no longer be issued as a standalone RFP document. USGS is working toward the following timeline for the RFP surrounding this scope of work: * Draft RFP Release: Estimating early February 2027 (anticipate this will be following spacecraft RFP award) * Industry briefing (virtual): Shortly after Draft RFP announcement * Feedback response period: Anticipated to be 30 days * Tentative one-on-one meetings with contractors as needed to clarify any feedback provided (could be virtual or in-person, at the government's discretion) * Final RFP Release: As soon as possible following updates to documentation based on industry feedback. Estimating May 2027

title: Remotely Operated Ground (UGV) and Aerial (UAV) Platforms with Ionizing Radiation Measurement Equipment
description: Procurement description As part of the Finnish RescEU project, the National Emergency Supply Agency (hereinafter "NESA") is preparing in cooperation with Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority (hereinafter "STUK") the procurement of remotely operated ground and aerial platforms equipped with ionizing radiation measurement devices. The equipment will be part of Finnish rescEU stockpile that is part of EU Civil Protection mechanism (UCPM). Countries that are part of the mechanism (“UCPM countries”) include all EU countries and participating countries that are Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Türkiye, Moldova and Ukraine. After emergency these countries can ask for assistance from the mechanism. In case of emergency, the stockpile would be activated and the devices would be sent to emergency area. The most probable end users would be first responders, security sector authorities (police, CBRN teams, defence forces) or rescue service personnel. According to preliminary estimates following quantities will be procured during 2026: - 20 - 30 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and RN sensor(s) (LOT A) - 4 - 8 tracked and/or wheeled UGVs and RN sensor(s) (LOT B) - 4 - 8 Quadruped UGVs and RN sensors (LOT C) Planned procurement schedule: 1. Request for proposal – November 2026 2. Deadline for tender questions – December 2026 3. Answers to tender questions – December 2026 4. Deadline for tenders – January 2027 5. Evaluation of tenders – January - February 2027 6. Procurement decision and notification to tenderers – March 2027 7. Procurement Agreement signing – March - April 2027, Tracked and/or wheeled UGVs and RN sensor(s) (LOT B) UGV (Unmanned Ground Vehicle) is a ground-based vehicle that operates without an onboard human operator and is controlled either remotely or autonomously by onboard systems. In the context of this procurement Lot, a UGV includes the ground platform, propulsion and mobility systems (tracks and/or wheels), navigation and control systems, communication links, power systems and any sensors, manipulators or payloads required for RN operations. The UGV system may comprise one or more UGV platforms, operator control units, communication links, support equipment, software, interfaces and accessories required for safe and effective operation. The UGV shall be suitable for professional operational use in RN monitoring, survey, inspection and reconnaissance tasks in varied and potentially hazardous environments. RN sensors (Radiological and Nuclear sensors) are devices designed for the detection, measurement, monitoring and/or radionuclide identification of ionizing radiation and radiological and nuclear materials. In the context of this procurement, an RN sensor includes the sensor unit, associated electronics, power interfaces, data acquisition and processing components, and any required firmware/software necessary for its intended operational use. The RN sensors shall be suitable for professional operational use and capable of supporting RN monitoring, survey, detection, identification or reconnaissance tasks under varying environmental and operational conditions. The tenderer shall deliver fully integrated and operational UGV and RN sensor combinations, demonstrated as functional systems prior to acceptance. The tenderer shall be fully responsible for ensuring the mechanical, electrical and functional integration of all platform and RN sensor components offered under the same Lot, regardless of whether these components are supplied by the tenderer or by subcontractors or consortium partners., Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and RN sensor(s) (LOT A) UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) is an aircraft that operates without a pilot on board and is controlled either remotely by a human operator or autonomously by onboard systems. In the context of this procurement, a UAV includes the aerial platform itself, its propulsion system, navigation and flight control systems, communication links, and any onboard sensors and payloads necessary for the intended operational use. The UAV shall be suitable for professional operational use and capable of performing missions related to radiological and nuclear (RN) monitoring, survey or reconnaissance tasks in varying environmental and operational conditions. The UAV may operate under visual line-of-sight (VLOS) or beyond visual line-of-sight (BVLOS) conditions subject to applicable European aviation regulations. RN sensors (Radiological and Nuclear sensors) are devices designed for the detection, measurement, monitoring and/or radionuclide identification of ionizing radiation and radiological and nuclear materials. In the context of this procurement, an RN sensor includes the sensor unit, associated electronics, power interfaces, data acquisition and processing components, and any required firmware/software necessary for its intended operational use. The RN sensors shall be suitable for professional operational use and capable of supporting RN monitoring, survey, detection, identification or reconnaissance tasks under varying environmental and operational conditions. The tenderer shall deliver fully integrated and operational UAV and RN sensor combinations, demonstrated as functional systems prior to acceptance. The tenderer shall be fully responsible for ensuring the mechanical, electrical and functional integration of all platform and RN sensor components offered under the same Lot, regardless of whether these components are supplied by the tenderer or by subcontractors or consortium partners., Quadruped UGVs and RN sensors (LOT C) UGV (Unmanned Ground Vehicle) is a ground-based vehicle that operates without an onboard human operator and is controlled either remotely or autonomously by onboard systems. In the context of this procurement Lot, a UGV includes the ground platform, propulsion and mobility systems (four (4) legs), navigation and control systems, communication links, power systems and any sensors, manipulators or payloads required for RN operations. The UGV system may comprise one or more UGV platforms, operator control units, communication links, support equipment, software, interfaces and accessories required for safe and effective operation. The UGV shall be suitable for professional operational use in RN monitoring, survey, inspection and reconnaissance tasks in varied and potentially hazardous environments. RN sensors (Radiological and Nuclear sensors) are devices designed for the detection, measurement, monitoring and/or radionuclide identification of ionizing radiation and radiological and nuclear materials. In the context of this procurement, an RN sensor includes the sensor unit, associated electronics, power interfaces, data acquisition and processing components, and any required firmware/software necessary for its intended operational use. The RN sensors shall be suitable for professional operational use and capable of supporting RN monitoring, survey, detection, identification or reconnaissance tasks under varying environmental and operational conditions. The tenderer shall deliver fully integrated and operational UGV and RN sensor combinations, demonstrated as functional systems prior to acceptance. The tenderer shall be fully responsible for ensuring the mechanical, electrical and functional integration of all platform and RN sensor components offered under the same Lot, regardless of whether these components are supplied by the tenderer or by subcontractors or consortium partners.,

description: Der JadeWeserPort in Wilhelmshaven ist der einzige tideunabhängige Container-Tiefwasserhafen an der deutschen Küste. In Angrenzung an das Containerterminal ist direkt auf dem aufgespülten Hafengroden das trimodale Gewerbegebiet entstanden, welches von der Container Terminal Wilhelmshaven JadeWeserPort-Marketing GmbH & Co. KG (im Folgenden: JWP-M) als Güterverkehrszentrum ("GVZ JadeWeserPort") entwickelt und betrieben wird. Diese Flächen sind durch die Gleisanlagen der Hafenbahn inkl. Vorstellgruppe, ein Umschlagterminal für den kombinierten Verkehr (KV) und die unmittelbar an dem GVZ JadeWeserPort endende BAB 29 an das europäische Verkehrsnetz angebunden. Ein Teil der derzeit noch nicht durch Vertragsschluss vergebenen Gewerbeflächen des GVZ JadeWeserPort mit einer Größe von ca. 264.000 m² (im Folgenden: Fläche E1) soll mit diesem Verhandlungsverfahren für gewerbliche/industrielle Ansiedlungen zur Errichtung und zum Betrieb von hafenaffinen Logistikimmobilien mittels Abschlusses eines Erbbaurechtsvertrages oder eines Mietvertrages (im Folgenden: Grundstücksvertrag) vergeben werden. Es sollen Unternehmen angesiedelt werden, die sich mit der Bearbeitung von ein- und ausgehenden Seegütern und/oder deren Lagerung und/oder Transport und/oder den damit verbundenen hafenaffinen Dienstleistungen beschäftigen. Es wird eine ausdrückliche Betriebspflicht in diesem Sinne vereinbart (hafenaffine Ansiedlung). Vorrangig sollen jedoch Unternehmen angesiedelt werden, die sich mit der Bearbeitung, der Lagerung und/oder dem Transport von Containern / containerisierten Gütern befassen.

title: RFP to Lease the Dun Glen Ark in New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
description: SUMMARY OF LEASING OPPORTUNITY This Request for Proposals (RFP) provides the opportunity for any interested individual or organization, hereinafter referred to as �Offeror� to submit proposals to the National Park Service (�NPS�, �Lessor�) to lease NPS property at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve (�New River Gorge�, �NERI�, �the Park�) for a Commercial Use under the following general terms and conditions. The selected Offeror (�offeror�, �you�, �your�) will have exclusive negotiation rights to enter into a lease based on the attached Sample Lease (See Attachment A). Elements of your proposal may be incorporated into the Lease at Lessor�s discretion. OBJECTIVES New River Gorge has seen a 40% increase in visitation since 2020. In 2023, the Park saw 1.71 million visitors and expects growth to continue into the coming years. Visitors to the national park spent ~$80 million in local communities around the park in 2021 and 2022, representing just a fraction of the $9 billion consumer spending on West Virginia outdoor recreation annually according to Outdoor Industry Association�s recreation economy report in 2022. New River Gorge has an extensive inventory of historic buildings throughout the park requiring rehabilitation and day-to-day maintenance. The Park is looking to revitalize these properties by seeking out qualified individuals to establish commercial businesses that are aligned to the Park�s mission and willing to take on all associated rehabilitation and maintenance costs. New River Gorge�s objective is to lease historic buildings to Lessees who demonstrate they can undertake rehabilitation of the structures in accordance with the Secretary of Interior�s Standards for the treatment of Historic Properties and demonstrate the financial capability to carry out the rehabilitation they propose to undertake. OVERVIEW OF THE PROPERTY OFFERED FOR LEASE The Dun Glen Ark, commonly known as the Ark, is located at 136 Dun Glen Parking Lot (McKendree Road), Thurmond, West Virginia, 25936 (37.95326077191746, -81.0755964412642). The lease premises solely includes the structural footprint of the Ark, Mini Ark, and Boat Storage Rack, while all surrounding property will be maintained by the Park for public use. The Ark is a two-story, approximately 3,276 sq. ft. structure with natural-stained wood siding and a second-floor balcony wrapping around the front (eastern, river-facing) side. A large garage door at the front allows for movement of watercraft and other large objects from the spacious single-bay ground floor directly onto the gravel Dun Glen river access road, about 50 feet from the boat ramp. The Mini Ark is a one-story approximately 984 sq. ft. structure built in a similar style to the Ark. The Mini Ark has three rooms, with inoperable restrooms in the back of the outside two. Room one is approximately 13� by 15�. Rooms two and three are approximately 12� by 20�. The Boat Storage Rack is an open air approximately 224 sq. ft. structure. The underside of the roof is 7-8 feet off the ground and 28� long by 9� wide. There are three support posts with three storage racks on each post. The lease premises include 0.41 acres of land as shown in Exhibit 1 below. The lease does not include reserved parking in the public parking lot, but parking could be added in the lease area next to the Mini Ark. The Ark was built in 1975 as part of the Wildwater Unlimited rafting company�s Dun Glen base of operations and originally used to house equipment in large bays on the ground floor and administrative offices above. From the turn of the 20th century through the next three decades, it was the site of the Dun Glen Hotel, which served the residents of the area as well as rail travelers passing through the town of Thurmond on the opposite bank of the river. Long after the hotel was destroyed by arson in 1930, the property passed into the ownership of Wildwater Unlimited, the first commercial rafting outfitter in West Virginia. The rafting company enjoyed many years of success before being acquired by a competitor, after which Dun Glen was sold to the NPS and transformed into a public day use area. Due to Dun Glen�s close affiliation with the establishment of the whitewater rafting industry in the state, the structures and the area are considered eligible for the National Register of Historic Places and must be treated similarly to other listed historic properties. The Mini Ark and Boat Storage Rack were added in 1985. The Ark lies fully within the Dun Glen Day Use Area, immediately adjacent to the main public boat launch into the New River. The Park�s priorities in Dun Glen are to maintain public access to the river and offer visitors a place to gather in close proximity to the area�s trails and the Thurmond Historic District. Dun Glen also serves as the gateway to Thurmond in the sense that it has better and more robust river access, parking capacity, event space, and utilities than available on the other side of the river. To reach Dun Glen, take U.S. Route 19 to the Glen Jean exit, north of Beckley. Follow the signs to Thurmond, seven miles down WV Route 25 (Route 25 is a narrow, winding road and is not recommended for RVs and trailers). Turn right onto the McKendree Road intersection immediately before crossing the Thurmond railroad bridge. Continue approximately 0.1 miles and the entrance to Dun Glen will be on the left along the river off McKendree Road. Park at the Upper Dun Glen Lot or continue along the river access road to the lower level to reach the Ark. From Dun Glen, Thurmond is 0.4 miles north across the railroad and auto bridge over the New River, the Stone Cliff Campground is 1.5 miles south down McKendree Road, the New River Gorge administrative headquarters is 6.4 miles west in the town of Glen Jean. The cities of Fayetteville and Beckley, WV are each located approximately 16 miles north and 19 miles south, respectively, along US Route 19. Allowed Uses of the Lease Premises The Ark is available for commercial use, this may include but is not limited to office space, tour operations, retail sale of consumer-packaged goods or other merchandise, rental of outdoor or other recreation equipment, or as an event venue (subject to NPS approval). The lessee may not use the premises for the following purposes: private use restricting access to the general public such as members-only clubs, illegal activities including but not limited to gambling, marijuana, or firearms, overnight lodging. Key Information About This Leasing Opportunity Deferred Maintenance: The roof of the Dun Glen Ark needs to be replaced, offerors willing to undertake this project should specify this in their proposal. A rental payment offset will be made available if a Lessee completes the work. Mail to: NERI_leasing@nps.gov. Building Codes and Zoning: The NPS will expect any work done on the property, where relevant, to meet the standards set forth by the 2024 ICC family of Codes and all codes referenced in those codes. For fire codes, follow all codes referenced in NPS Director�s Order #58 and NPS Reference Manual #58. For accessibility, work must meet the ICC Codes and the Architectural Barriers Act Accessibility Standard (ABAAS). Additionally, Certificates of Occupancy are issued by the NPS Building Code Official. Historic Preservation: Construction design, authorization, regulatory compliance, and permitting will be required to comply with one or several of the following: the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines; National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) and Section 106 compliance; National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); NFPA 914 Code for Protection of Historical Structures. Please note that your proposal may trigger compliance processes in accordance with one or more of the laws, regulations or policies listed above. The cost of any such compliance process as well as the costs of plan check, code review and construction inspections will be borne by the Lessee. Pu

title: RESERVE BASIN MAINTENANCE DREDGING CONTRACT FOR SITES AT THE PHILDELPHIA NAVY YARD IN THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT PENNSYLVANIA AREA OF RESPONSIBILIY
description: The project consists of Maintenance Dredging within the North Side (Wharf N) of Reserve Basin and Schuylkill River Access Channel for the Government sites at the Philadelphia Navy Yard in the Public Works Department Pennsylvania area of responsibility. Maintenance dredging of approximately 96,611 cubic yards of sediment, using a sealed environmental clamshell bucket. Dredging within the Reserve Basin is in support of the Naval Support Activity Mechanicsburg, Philadelphia Navy Yard Annex. The Reserve Basin is being used to decommission various US Naval vessels. For the river pilots to be able to safely maneuver vessels through the Schuylkill River into the Reserve Basin berths and to ensure that tidal cycles will not cause sediment accumulation around the hulls making final removal very difficult, the berths need to be dredged to a minimum depth of -30 MLLW and a maximum over-dredge depth of -32 MLLW.

title: Pre Solicitation: Residential Reentry Center and Home Confinement Services within city limits of Harrisburg, PA. Home Confinement within Radius 120 Miles of the Facility
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000023 Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the city limits of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Home Confinement Radius 120 miles within RRC Facility The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the city limits of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Home Confinement Radius 120 miles of RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 15 beds (15 males and 0 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 30 beds (26 males and 4 females) for facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 13 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 25 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000023 will be available on or about November 16, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around January 15, 2027. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. title: Remplacement de 76 moniteurs de surveillance / défibrillateurs
description:
Les appareils de surveillance et de réanimation utilisés par le SRZ dans le cadre des services de secours et de transfert, ainsi que lors de grands événements et de catastrophes, constituent un élément central des soins préhospitaliers. Ces appareils sont utilisés au quotidien à bord des ambulances et des véhicules de secours, et font partie du stock de remplacement disponible dans les différents postes. Les appareils les plus anciens sont conservés dans le stock de matériel destiné aux catastrophes.


Une partie du parc actuel d’appareils a déjà dépassé la durée de vie prévue de 10 ans ou l’atteindra dans les prochaines années. C’est pourquoi le parc d’appareils doit être remplacé au cours des prochaines années par de nouveaux systèmes modernes. Outre le remplacement des appareils, cette appel d’offres porte également sur la disponibilité d’accessoires et de consommables adaptés aux moniteurs de surveillance des patients / défibrillateurs, la mise en service et la maintenance des appareils, ainsi que la formation des utilisateurs et utilisatrices.


Les exigences détaillées et les spécifications techniques figurent dans le dossier d’appel d’offres.

title: Accords-cadres « Prestations de contrôle en génie civil et infrastructures »
description:
Swissgrid exploite, entretient et développe le réseau suisse de transport d’électricité. Dans le cadre de projets de construction, de transformation et de rénovation de lignes et de postes électriques, des prestations de contrôle indépendantes sont nécessaires afin de garantir la vérification technique des calculs statiques, des justificatifs structurels ainsi que des documents d’exécution. En raison de l’augmentation du nombre et de la complexité des projets, ces prestations seront à l’avenir partiellement confiées à des ingénieurs contrôleurs externes.


Le présent appel d’offres a pour objet la conclusion d’accords-cadres pour des prestations de contrôle statique dans les domaines du bâtiment et du génie civil, couvrant les phases « projet d’ouvrage » ainsi que « projet d’exécution et réalisation ». L’appel d’offres est subdivisé en quatre lots :


• Lot 1 : Génie civil, fondations de pylônes pour les lignes électriques – allemand

• Lot 2 : Génie civil, fondations de pylônes pour les lignes électriques – français

• Lot 3 : Bâtiment, ouvrages des postes électriques – allemand

• Lot 4 : Bâtiment, ouvrages des postes électriques – français


L’attribution des mandats de contrôle s’effectuera, pendant la durée des accords-cadres, selon les besoins et au moyen de mini-appels d’offres (mini-tenders) organisés entre les partenaires contractuels sélectionnés pour le lot concerné. Aucun volume minimal de prestations n’est garanti.


L’objectif des accords-cadres est de garantir des prestations de contrôle de haute qualité, indépendantes et efficaces, ainsi que l’identification précoce des risques et des potentiels d’optimisation dans les projets de Swissgrid.
